# lesson 4 of T5.4 Theory: Production concerns: batching, caching and similarity behaviour

## Embedding cache

Every re-run of an indexing notebook, and every re-ingest after a change elsewhere in the pipeline, embeds the whole corpus again and pays for it again, for vectors identical to the ones you already had. `CacheBackedEmbeddings` wraps any embedding model with a key-value store: text it has seen comes back from the store, and only new text reaches the model.

```python
from langchain_classic.embeddings import CacheBackedEmbeddings   # LangChain 1.x; 0.x: langchain.embeddings
from langchain_classic.storage import LocalFileStore             # 0.x: langchain.storage

cached = CacheBackedEmbeddings.from_bytes_store(
    underlying_embeddings=OpenAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-3-small"),
    document_embedding_cache=LocalFileStore("./.embedding_cache/"),
    namespace="text-embedding-3-small:1536:",   # model and dimensions
    key_encoder="sha256",                        # the default, sha1, warns
)
```

The key is the namespace followed by a hash of the text, so a cache entry matches only the exact text under the exact namespace. To see what that means for the Larkspur handbook, the 12 chunks of the [T5.1](../m10_rag_lifecycle/00_overview.md) lab were run through the real `CacheBackedEmbeddings` with a counting stand-in for the API (LangChain's `DeterministicFakeEmbedding`, so the counts are exact and free):

| Run | Texts sent to the model | Keys in the store |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Index the 12 chunks | 12 of 12 | 12 |
| 2. Index the same 12 again | 0 of 12, identical vectors | 12 |
| 3. Edit one chunk ("100 GB" to "200 GB"), index again | 1 of 12 | 13 |
| 4. A second model under its own namespace | 12 of 12 | 25 |
| 5. A second model, both with no namespace | 0 of 12: every vector is the first model's | 12, shared by both |

- **Re-indexing after an edit costs the edit.** When [T5.3](../m12_chunking/00_overview.md)'s chunking changes only some chunks, only those are embedded again; chunks whose text is unchanged hit the cache.
- **Old entries stay.** Run 3 leaves the pre-edit vector in the store. A file store grows until you clear it, so give it a home you can delete or expire.
- **The namespace is part of correctness.** `from_bytes_store` defaults to an empty namespace. Run 5 swaps the model and gets the old model's vectors back with no error, an index mixing two vector spaces, which is the mismatch from [lesson 1 of T5.4](01_embedding_fundamentals_similarity_metrics_and_model_selection.md#lesson-the-same-model-on-both-sides). Put the model name and its `dimensions` setting in the namespace.

Only documents are cached by default (`query_embedding_cache=False`), which suits most traffic, since few queries repeat word for word. `LocalFileStore` writes one file per vector; for a cache shared between workers, any other `ByteStore`, such as Redis, works the same way. Notebook 4 of T5.4 uses a `TemporaryDirectory`, so its cache is discarded when the cell ends.

## Batching

`embed_documents(texts)` sends many texts in one request; `embed_query(text)` sends one. Looping `embed_query` over a corpus pays one network round trip per chunk, and on a real corpus that is the difference between minutes and hours. Use `embed_documents` for the index and `embed_query` for questions.

Notebook 1 of T5.4 runs both paths on the same six texts and compares the vectors. They are semantically identical (cosine about 1.0) but not bit-identical, because a batched request and a single request take different paths through the server. The difference is numerical noise, so never use exact equality to decide whether two vectors came from the same text; that is the cache's job. For an asymmetric model the two methods differ on purpose, which is one more reason to keep the two calls separate (lesson 3 of T5.4).

## Key Takeaways

- `CacheBackedEmbeddings` keys each vector on namespace plus a hash of the text, so re-indexing after an edit pays only for the changed chunks. Old entries stay until you clear them.
- Put the model name and `dimensions` in the cache namespace. The default empty namespace silently returns the old model's vectors after a model swap.
- Embed the corpus with batched `embed_documents`, not a loop of `embed_query`. The two paths differ by numerical noise, so never compare vectors for exact equality.

`embed_documents` sends many texts in one request, while looping `embed_query` pays one network round trip per chunk, the difference between minutes and hours on a real corpus. The two paths return vectors that are semantically identical (cosine about 1.0) but not bit-identical, because they take different paths through the server. <details>
<summary>2. You edit one of the 12 Larkspur chunks from 100 GB to 200 GB and re-index through the cache. How many texts reach the model, and how many keys are stored?</summary>

One of 12 texts reaches the model, and the store holds 13 keys. The edited text hashes to a new key, and the pre-edit vector stays in the store, which grows until you clear it.

</details>

<details>
<summary>3. After you swap embedding models, re-indexing sends zero texts to the model and retrieval quality collapses. What is wrong?</summary>

Both models share the default empty namespace of `from_bytes_store`, so the cache returns the first model's vectors for the second model's requests. The index now mixes two vector spaces, with no error. Put the model name and its `dimensions` setting in the namespace.

</details>
